hypothesis: The neuron selects for **concentric circular patterns and bullseye-like geometries**, most strongly activated by **close-up views of eyes** and **round, convex objects** that mimic an eye structure. The core visual feature is a **dark, central circular spot** (typically a pupil, mechanical hub, or target center) enclosed by a **contrasting, often glossy ring or spherical body** (such as an iris, orbital skin, plastic flange, or insect carapace). The surrounding features frequently exhibit **warm, saturated colors**—specifically **tangerine-orange, amber, yellow, deep red, or gold**—or high-contrast **cream and white**, set against the **jet-black** central element. The background is typically **out-of-focus** and composed of natural or neutral tones like **muted green, weathered brown, or grey**, providing a soft contrast to the sharp, glossy subject. The activating feature typically occupies **30–70% of the image frame** and is positioned **centrally or slightly off-center**. The neuron remains invariant to the semantic category—responding to birds, reptiles, insects, and mechanical objects alike—as long as the **strong dark-center/bright-surround contrast** and **circular morphology** are preserved.
